database_summary: This SQLite schema models geographic/political entities (states, cities) and related physical features (borders, high/low points, lakes, mountains, rivers). Tables mostly describe entities and their attributes. There are several one-to-many relationships implied (e.g., a state can have many lakes, rivers traverse states, a state can border many other states). No temporal/versioning columns are present. Row counts in the provided profile are zero for all tables, so no sampled data distributions are available beyond declared types and declared primary keys/foreign keys.

accepted.name: state_base
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  state_name,
  population,
  area,
  country_name,
  capital,
  density,
  CASE
    WHEN density IS NOT NULL THEN density
    WHEN population IS NOT NULL AND area IS NOT NULL AND area != 0 THEN (CAST(population AS REAL) / area)
    ELSE NULL
  END AS population_density
FROM state
accepted.description: Normalized projection of the state table preserving original columns and exposing a derived population_density ratio when density is missing. Use when questions need state-level attributes or a canonical state relation for joins. | Use for: List states with population or density; compute per-state population density; join state attributes to city/river/lake features.

accepted.name: city_base
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  city_name,
  population,
  country_name,
  state_name
FROM city
accepted.description: Projection of city rows preserving identifying columns and population measure. Use when questions need city-level attributes or to join cities to their states. | Use for: Top cities by population within a state or country; counts of cities per state; join to state attributes.

accepted.name: lakes_by_state
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  state_name,
  COUNT(*) AS lake_count,
  SUM(area) AS total_lake_area
FROM lake
GROUP BY state_name
accepted.description: Aggregated measures of lakes per state: count of lakes and total lake area. Use when questions ask about number or total area of lakes per state or need to rank states by lake presence. | Use for: Which states have the most lakes; which states have the largest total lake area; filter states by lake_count or total_lake_area thresholds.

accepted.name: mountain_stats_by_state
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  state_name,
  COUNT(*) AS mountain_count,
  MAX(mountain_altitude) AS max_mountain_altitude,
  AVG(mountain_altitude) AS avg_mountain_altitude
FROM mountain
GROUP BY state_name
accepted.description: Per-state aggregated mountain statistics: number of mountains, max altitude, average altitude. Useful for comparing mountainousness across states or filtering states by mountain measures. | Use for: Top states by highest mountain; average mountain altitude by state; states with no mountains (via left join to state).

accepted.name: state_with_city_counts
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  s.state_name,
  s.population,
  s.area,
  s.country_name,
  s.capital,
  COUNT(c.city_name) AS city_count,
  MAX(c.population) AS max_city_population
FROM state s
LEFT JOIN city c ON c.state_name = s.state_name
GROUP BY s.state_name, s.population, s.area, s.country_name, s.capital
accepted.description: Denormalized relation joining states to the count of cities in each state plus largest city population. Use when questions require state attributes alongside city-derived measures. | Use for: Compare states by number of cities; find states where largest city exceeds a threshold; list state attributes with city counts.

accepted.name: state_border_neighbors
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  b.state_name,
  b.border,
  s1.population AS population,
  s1.country_name AS country_name,
  s1.capital AS capital,
  s2.population AS neighbor_population,
  s2.country_name AS neighbor_country_name,
  s2.capital AS neighbor_capital
FROM border_info b
LEFT JOIN state s1 ON b.state_name = s1.state_name
LEFT JOIN state s2 ON b.border = s2.state_name
accepted.description: Each row is a bordering pair with attributes for the source state and the neighbor state (denormalized). Useful for questions about neighbor counts, neighbor attributes, or graph analyses when combined with aggregation or recursive CTEs. | Use for: Count neighbors per state; list neighbor attributes; find cross-country borders by comparing country_name and neighbor_country_name.

accepted.name: river_traverse_expanded
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  r.river_name,
  r.length,
  r.country_name,
  r.traverse,
  s.population AS state_population,
  s.area AS state_area,
  s.country_name AS state_country_name
FROM river r
LEFT JOIN state s ON r.traverse = s.state_name
accepted.description: Rivers joined to the state they traverse, exposing state attributes alongside river measures. Use when questions ask about rivers by state or need to filter rivers by state-level properties. | Use for: List rivers traversing a given state; aggregate river lengths by state; find rivers whose state attributes meet conditions.

accepted.name: cities_ranked_within_state
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  city_name,
  population,
  country_name,
  state_name,
  RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY state_name ORDER BY population DESC) AS rank_by_state
FROM city
accepted.description: Ranks cities within each state by population (largest = rank 1). Use to implement top-K city queries per state by applying a downstream WHERE rank_by_state <= K. | Use for: Top N cities by population within each state; find the capital's rank within its state by population.

accepted.name: states_running_lake_area
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  state_name,
  lake_count,
  total_lake_area,
  SUM(COALESCE(total_lake_area,0)) OVER (ORDER BY state_name ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS running_total_lake_area
FROM (
  SELECT state_name, COUNT(*) AS lake_count, SUM(area) AS total_lake_area
  FROM lake
  GROUP BY state_name
) sub
accepted.description: Per-state running total of lake area ordered by state_name. Useful for cumulative-distribution style questions across an ordered list of states (alphabetical or other ORDER BY can be replaced downstream). | Use for: Compute cumulative lake area across states ordered by name or other attribute; find percentile cutoffs when combined with total sum.

accepted.name: state_highlow_joined
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  s.state_name,
  s.population,
  s.area,
  s.country_name,
  s.capital,
  h.highest_elevation,
  h.lowest_elevation,
  h.highest_point,
  h.lowest_point
FROM state s
LEFT JOIN highlow h ON s.state_name = h.state_name
accepted.description: State attributes joined with their high/low point textual descriptors. Use when questions need elevation descriptors alongside state details. | Use for: Retrieve highest/lowest point descriptions alongside state metadata; filter states by presence/absence of high/low info.

accepted.name: state_neighbor_counts
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  state_name,
  COUNT(DISTINCT border) AS neighbor_count
FROM border_info
GROUP BY state_name
accepted.description: Count of distinct neighbors per state based on border_info. Useful for ranking or filtering states by number of bordering states. | Use for: Which states border the most other states; filter states by neighbor_count; map cross-country neighboring states by joining to state table.
